title.value: Preference for biological motion is reduced in ASD: implications for clinical trials and the search for biomarkers
title.justification: The title clearly summarizes the main focus of the paper, which investigates the differences in preference for biological motion in individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and its implications.
title.quote: Preference for biological motion is reduced in ASD: implications for clinical trials and the search for biomarkers

analysis.description: The paper investigates the differences in preference for biological motion between individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) and neurotypical individuals, utilizing eye-tracking data from a large sample of autistic and non-autistic participants. This research aims to understand how biological motion preference is modulated by factors such as age and sex, and its association with ASD symptomatology, providing insights for clinical trials and biomarker search.

type.justification: The paper presents data collected from experiments involving eye-tracking of individuals with ASD and neurotypical controls to study biological motion preference.
type.quote: Eye-tracking data were collected from 486 6-to-30-year-old autistic (N = 282) and non-autistic control (N = 204) participants...

name.justification: The paper is centered around understanding autism spectrum disorder (ASD) through behavioral differences in biological motion preference as a potential biomarker.
name.quote: ...focusing on perception of biological motion, a promising index of social brain function which may be altered in ASD.

name.justification: The research involves understanding the neurocognitive mechanisms related to social brain function through biological motion perception.
name.quote: These networks generate representations of the complex kinematics associated with human action and gesture which form the basis for more advanced social cognitive processes...

name.justification: The research addresses behavioral aspects and symptomatology related to ASD, which connects to psychological research domains.
name.quote: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a lifelong pervasive developmental condition, characterised by social-communication and interaction difficulties...

name.justification: The eye-tracking data used in the paper comes from the LEAP study, which involved a substantial number of participants across different age ranges.
name.quote: Eye-tracking data were collected in the context of the EU-AIMS Longitudinal European Autism Project (LEAP)
